# Architecture Requirements Quality Checklist: Synthia Platform Engineering Scaffold

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing the platform's load-bearing guarantees are
complete, clear, consistent and measurable — before implementation begins.
**Created**: 2026-09-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does **not** mean implementation work is complete.

> **This checklist cannot be used to claim the scaffold is built.** Every item asks whether a
> requirement is *written well*, never whether the system *works*. A fully checked file means the
> specification is ready to implement against — nothing more.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for thumbs-up/down feedback, covering capture, revision, scope and its exclusion from any decision path? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SESS-009]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: gap addressed. Spec FR-SESS-009 to FR-SESS-014 added (per-message, revisable, owner-scoped, aggregate reporting, never a decision input, retention). `data-model.md` gained a Feedback entity; `contracts/customer-api.md` corrected from a session-scoped `POST` to a message-scoped `PUT`/`DELETE`. Reviewer to confirm the requirements now read correctly.
- [x] CHK002 Is the destination of an escalated request specified — which queue, role or system receives it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-FALL-002]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: gap addressed. FR-FALL-002 to FR-FALL-006 added — escalation goes to the ServiceNow queue with transcript, candidates and reason, never requires approval, and is audited. The wider gap this exposed is also closed: FR-EXT-001 to FR-EXT-007 now state ServiceNow as system of record, case creation at the triage gate, idempotent write-backs, and inbound state changes as untrusted. The *specific* queue mapping remains an inherited open item and is recorded under Dependencies.
- [x] CHK003 Are per-organisation rate limiting or budget requirements documented, given the platform serves many customers from one deployment? [Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-OPS-005 and FR-OPS-006 — per-organisation token, compute and request budgets, with a throttled response reported distinctly from a failure.
- [x] CHK004 Are observability requirements specified at the behavioural level, or does the spec cover only audit and leave telemetry entirely to the constitution? [Gap, Spec §FR-AUDIT-001]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by the new FR-OPS group — correlation propagation, the three telemetry pillars tagged from trusted context, agent-specific signals, and an explicit prohibition on answering an audit question with telemetry.
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements defined for what a user sees while work is suspended for hours or days? [Gap, Coverage]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SESS-018 — a suspended session is visible to its user as awaiting them, naming which interruption is pending, both in the session and in their listing.
- [x] CHK006 Are loading, empty and partial-failure state requirements defined for the three client surfaces? [Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SURF-016 and SC-SURF-004 — loading, empty and partial-failure states defined per primary journey, and a failure never rendered as an empty result.
- [x] CHK007 Are session and work-item lifecycle states enumerated in the specification itself, or only in the downstream data model? [Completeness, Traceability]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SESS-015 to FR-SESS-017 — the nine session states are now enumerated in the spec itself, with the three awaiting states persisting indefinitely.
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* **FR-EXEC-010** added, enumerating the nine work-item states and the five approval states, and stating that the two are independent so an approved-but-unexecuted item is distinguishable. Session states were already enumerated by FR-SESS-015. A four-value `chat_session.state` enum in `data-model.md` that contradicted FR-SESS-015 was found during the fix and corrected.
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for how a user discovers that a suspended session is waiting on them after they have left the client? [Gap, Coverage]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SESS-018 and FR-SESS-019 — visibility in the session listing, and rebuild-from-platform on reconnect rather than from missed notifications.
- [x] CHK009 Does the specification state what the scaffold does when the governance catalogue contains only reference fixtures and a user asks for something real? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SCOPE-008]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: already covered by FR-SCOPE-008 and FR-FALL-009 — with no use case defined, every action-requiring request routes to manual resolution.

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK010 Is "genuine problem" defined with criteria a reviewer could apply consistently, or does the triage gate rest on an undefined judgement? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-SESS-003]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed — FR-SESS-003 now defines a genuine problem as a turn that states a problem or requests an action, excluding greetings, small talk and meta-conversation.
- [x] CHK011 Is "explicit and visible" fallback quantified, or could a silently-logged escalation satisfy the wording? [Clarity, Spec §FR-FALL-007]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed — FR-FALL-007 now requires the fallback to be stated in the conversation and recorded on the case; a log entry alone does not satisfy it.
- [x] CHK012 Can "conveyed to assistive technology" be objectively verified, or does it need a named success criterion? [Measurability, Spec §FR-SURF-011]
- [x] CHK013 Is "without flooding the user with repeated announcements" measurable, or is it a subjective threshold? [Measurability, Spec §FR-SURF-011]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* FR-SURF-011 rewritten to the testable form: announce **only text not already announced**, never re-announce. The unmeasurable word "flooding" is gone, and the rule a test can assert — no duplicate announcement of already-announced content — is now the requirement rather than a restatement buried in a contract.
- [x] CHK014 Are the four execution treatments defined somewhere the specification references, rather than assumed known? [Clarity, Traceability]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* A four-row **Execution treatment** table added to the Requirements preamble, naming `AUTO`, `END_USER_APPROVAL`, `STAFF_APPROVAL` and `NOT_ALLOWED`, citing `Synthia-Platform-Specification.md` §4.3 as their definition, and stating the set is closed and assigned from the catalogue. Nothing is redefined here.
- [x] CHK015 Is "inert" defined for reference operations with testable criteria — no external call, no state change, or both? [Clarity, Spec §FR-SCOPE-005]
- [x] CHK016 Is "context preserved" on escalation specified concretely enough that a reviewer could tell whether a handoff satisfied it? [Measurability, Spec §FR-FALL-008]
- [x] CHK017 Are the success criteria free of terms that cannot be objectively evaluated at release? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK018 Do the specification and `contracts/customer-api.md` agree on the full set of customer operations, including operations added after the contracts were first written? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK019 Are the retention windows stated in the spec consistent with those in `data-model.md` and ADR-0003? [Consistency, Spec §FR-SESS-007]
- [x] CHK020 Is the read-only rule for the query-side deployable stated consistently, with no requirement implying it accepts a write? [Consistency, plan.md §Dependency direction]
- [x] CHK021 Do the requirements use one canonical term per concept, avoiding drift between "organisation" and "tenant" across sections? [Consistency, Terminology]
- [x] CHK022 Are the three interruption types named identically in the spec, the contracts and the data model? [Consistency, Spec §FR-INTR-001]
- [x] CHK023 Do accessibility requirements apply consistently to all three surfaces, with no surface implicitly exempted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-SURF-010]
- [x] CHK024 Is the verification vocabulary (`server_confirmed` / `client_attested` / `contradicted`) used identically in the spec, contracts and ADR-0004? [Consistency]

## Authorization Rules

- [x] CHK025 Is the prohibition on ranking, sorting or comparing roles stated as a requirement, not merely implied by "set intersection"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-AUTHZ-003]
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for what happens when an operation declares no accepted roles at all? [Edge Case, Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-AUTHZ-010 — an empty accepted-role set is a total denial, never an implicit allow.
- [x] CHK027 Is it specified that every operation must declare its accepted role set explicitly, with no default? [Completeness, Spec §FR-AUTHZ-005]
- [x] CHK028 Are the customer and staff authorization models stated as separate in a way that prevents a rule written for one being reused for the other? [Clarity, Spec §FR-AUTHZ-009]
- [x] CHK029 Is the surface-determines-persona rule stated as a requirement rather than left to the identity section to imply? [Completeness, ADR-0001]
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for a staff member whose roles change while a session or approval is in flight? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-AUTHZ-011 — decisions are evaluated against roles held at decision time and record that set; a later role change neither rewrites a decision nor cancels authorized work.
- [x] CHK031 Is it specified that role checks in a client are presentation-only *and* that the server re-decides, rather than only the first half? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SURF-004]

## Tenant Isolation

- [x] CHK032 Are isolation requirements stated for every tier named — API, application, database, cache, messaging, retrieval and audit — or only for retrieval? [Coverage, Spec §FR-IDENT-008]
- [x] CHK033 Is the requirement that no unfiltered query path may *exist* distinguished from a requirement that queries *are* filtered? [Clarity, Spec §FR-IDENT-009]
- [x] CHK034 Is the choice of 404 over 403 for another organisation's resource stated as a requirement with its rationale, so it is not "corrected" later? [Completeness, Traceability]
- [x] CHK035 Are requirements defined for cross-organisation exposure through aggregate or dashboard data, where individual records are not returned but counts might leak? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-IDENT-010 and a dedicated aggregate-leakage test — counts, rankings and distributions must not reveal a single organisation's contribution.
- [x] CHK036 Is the zero-exposure release gate stated with a defined scope — which paths must be swept before a release qualifies? [Measurability, Spec §SC-IDENT-002]

## Interruption & Resume Behaviour

- [x] CHK037 Are requirements defined for all three interruption types with equal specificity, or is clarification treated more loosely than consent and approval? [Consistency, Spec §FR-INTR-001]
- [x] CHK038 Is "suspends durably and for an unbounded period" bounded anywhere by a competing requirement such as retention? [Conflict, Spec §FR-INTR-002]
- [x] CHK039 Are requirements defined for a session suspended longer than its content-retention window? [Edge Case, Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SESS-020 — retention now runs from the terminal state, so a session suspended indefinitely cannot lose the context it is suspended on. data-model.md updated to match.
- [x] CHK040 Is it specified that resume continues the stream rather than restarting, in a way that is observably testable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-INTR-012]
- [x] CHK041 Are requirements defined for two decisions arriving concurrently for the same interrupt beyond the approval case — for instance two technicians taking over one session? [Gap, Edge Case]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-INTR-013 — concurrent take-over resolves to one owner, the later attempt recorded without changing ownership.
- [ ] CHK042 Is the behaviour specified when a trigger arrives but the checkpoint is not at the expected position? [Gap, Spec Dependencies]
  - *Finding 2026-09-16 — still open, correctly.* Re-verified. Unchanged: OQ-08 is unresolved upstream and `docs/adr/0002` §Unresolved and `research.md` §Outstanding both carry it. It sits on the Phase 13 critical path (T117, resume worker). Meet it as a decision at Phase 13; do not let it be discovered there.
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: NOT closed, and not closable here. Trigger/checkpoint reconciliation is an inherited open item in the platform specification (OQ-08). Closing it locally would invent upstream architecture.
- [x] CHK043 Are requirements defined for cancelling work that is suspended at a clarification rather than at an approval? [Coverage, Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-INTR-014 — cancellation is available at every suspension point, not only while awaiting approval.

## Realtime Non-Authority

- [x] CHK044 Is the requirement that the realtime channel confers no authority stated positively — what it *may* carry — as well as negatively? [Clarity, Spec §FR-IDENT-005]
- [x] CHK045 Is it required that a client re-authorizes through an API rather than acting on a notification, or only that the channel does not authorize? [Completeness, Coverage]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SURF-018 — a client must not treat a notification as authority; any action it prompts goes through an independently authorized request.
- [x] CHK046 Are requirements defined for what a notification envelope may contain, so "no authority-bearing value" is enforceable rather than aspirational? [Measurability, contracts/notifications.md]
- [x] CHK047 Are requirements defined for behaviour when the realtime channel is unavailable, and do they confirm nothing is authorized differently? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK048 Is the distinction between delivering a prompt and delivering a decision stated explicitly enough that an implementer could not conflate them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-INTR-003]

## RagCore / .NET Separation

- [x] CHK049 Is the no-application-dependency rule stated in both directions, with the forms it forbids (API call, library reference, deployment coupling) enumerated? [Completeness, plan.md §Dependency direction, ADR-0001]
- [x] CHK050 Are the permitted meeting points — shared database and asynchronous messaging — stated as an exhaustive list rather than examples? [Clarity, plan.md §Dependency direction, ADR-0001]
- [x] CHK051 Is the schema-as-contract consequence stated as a requirement, given no architecture test can detect a breach of it? [Completeness, ADR-0001]
- [x] CHK052 Is the view versioning rule specified with the prohibition on altering a view in place, not only the convention to add a new version? [Clarity, contracts/read-views.md]
- [x] CHK053 Are requirements defined for how a client discovers which backend serves a given operation, or is routing left entirely to the gateway configuration? [Gap, Coverage]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-SURF-017 — a client addresses one gateway and is never configured with more than one platform origin; which backend serves an operation is not a client concern.

## Manual Fallback

- [x] CHK054 Is it stated that every action-requiring request falls back while no use case is defined, rather than leaving that as an inference? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SCOPE-008]
- [x] CHK055 Are the prohibited fallback behaviours enumerated — silent degradation, stubbed success, fabricated result — rather than covered by a general honesty clause? [Clarity, Spec §FR-FALL-007]
- [x] CHK056 Are requirements defined for fallback when the escalation target itself is unavailable? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-FALL-005]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-FALL-005 — the escalation queues and replays, is never silently dropped, and the user is still told a human will take the request.
- [x] CHK057 Is it specified whether a user is told *why* the platform cannot proceed, or only *that* it cannot? [Clarity, Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-FALL-010 — the user is told why the platform could not proceed, not only that it could not.

## Integration Boundaries

- [x] CHK058 Is "discovery is not entitlement" stated as a requirement with both conditions for callability — registration *and* entitlement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-EXT-014]
- [x] CHK059 Are requirements defined for third-party output that is malformed or hostile, beyond the rule that output is data rather than instruction? [Coverage, Spec §FR-EXT-017]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-EXT-021 — malformed, oversized or contract-violating third-party output is rejected at the boundary and never reaches the agent loop or domain.
- [x] CHK060 Is the extensibility requirement measurable — could a reviewer objectively determine that adding a system required no new authorization mechanism? [Measurability, Spec §SC-EXT-002]
- [x] CHK061 Are requirements defined for behaviour when a third-party system is entitled but unreachable, distinct from unavailable-and-unentitled? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-EXT-020]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed by FR-EXT-022 — entitled-but-unreachable is reported distinctly from not-entitled, and neither as a failure of the user's request.
- [x] CHK062 Is the prohibition on provider vocabulary leaking inward stated in a way that can be reviewed, rather than only asserted? [Measurability, Spec §FR-EXT-011]
- [x] CHK063 Are credential-handling requirements complete — per organisation, per system, never surfaced in conversation, step trail, telemetry or audit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-EXT-016]

## Testing Requirements

- [x] CHK064 Are the required test classes stated in the specification itself, or does the spec rely on the constitution to carry them? [Traceability, Completeness]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed — the spec now names the verification classes and points at the constitution as the single governing list, rather than silently relying on it.
- [x] CHK065 Is it specified which changes trigger which test class, so "a security fix needs a test" is actionable rather than a slogan? [Clarity, Gap]
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* Constitution **v3.1.0** adds *Which change requires which category* — a twelve-row table mapping change type to owed test categories, so the obligation is mechanical at review rather than judgement. Same fix closes `implementation.md` CHK085.
- [x] CHK066 Are the acceptance scenarios written so each maps to at least one required test class? [Traceability, Coverage]
- [x] CHK067 Is the requirement for a failing-then-passing test on isolation and security fixes stated as a merge condition? [Measurability]
- [x] CHK068 Are requirements defined for how the four reference operations are used to exercise the governance paths, given three user stories depend on them? [Completeness, Spec §FR-SCOPE-004]

## Unresolved Requirements & Deferrals

- [x] CHK069 Is every deferred item recorded with the cost of deferring it, rather than only the decision to defer? [Completeness, Spec Dependencies]
- [x] CHK070 Does each deferral name the condition or event that would force it to be revisited? [Clarity, Gap]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed — each deferral in Dependencies now carries an explicit *Revisit when* condition.
  - *Closed 2026-09-16.* A labelled ***Revisit when:*** condition added to the six deferrals that lacked one — product definitions, enterprise identity, endpoint execution safeguards, second-approval behaviour, residency retrofit and queue routing. All eight deferrals now carry one, so the 2026-09-15 finding is true as written for the first time.
- [x] CHK071 Are the inherited open items from the platform specification listed with their impact on this feature, rather than referenced in bulk? [Traceability, Spec Dependencies]
- [x] CHK072 Is it unambiguous which non-binding performance targets are excluded from acceptance, so none can be mistaken for a gate? [Clarity, Spec §PT-001–PT-003]
- [x] CHK073 Are the security-critical open items blocking the endpoint execution path flagged in the spec itself and not only in ADR-0004? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK074 Is the absence of a scale envelope recorded as a deliberate omission rather than left silent? [Assumption, Gap]
- [x] CHK075 Are assumptions stated in a falsifiable form, so a reviewer could identify when one has become untrue? [Measurability, Spec Assumptions]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK076 Are requirements defined for the primary flow of every user story, including the one with the fewest acceptance scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §US4]
- [x] CHK077 Are exception and recovery flows specified for each interruption type, not only the happy path? [Coverage, Gap]
- [x] CHK078 Are requirements defined for organisation suspension or offboarding occurring mid-session? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK079 Are requirements defined for the boundary cases grouped as one — duplicate triggers, expiry without execution, cancellation after claim, and revoked requester access? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK080 Is a requirement and acceptance-criteria identifier scheme established and used consistently across spec, contracts and tasks? [Traceability]
  - *Finding 2026-09-15*: addressed. Positional `FR-NNN` numbering was replaced with stable
    `FR-<GROUP>-<NNN>` IDs, governed by a never-renumber / never-reuse / append-within-group rule
    stated in the spec. The migration exposed that most downstream citations had been silently wrong
    for several revisions; all were re-verified against requirement text and corrected. Success
    criteria were migrated the same way to `SC-<GROUP>-<NNN>`, reusing the requirement group names so a
    criterion can be matched to the requirements it measures. `PT-` stays distinct so non-binding
    targets can never be mistaken for acceptance criteria.

## Review record

**Reviewed 2026-09-16.** All 80 items assessed against `spec.md`, `Synthia-Platform-Specification.md`,
constitution v3.0.0 (since amended to **v3.1.0**, which is what closed CHK065), `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `data-model.md`, `research.md`, `contracts/` and
`docs/adr/0001-0005`.

**Result: 79 of 80 satisfied.** Five of the six items open at first review were closed on 2026-09-16
by amending the artifacts — CHK007 (FR-EXEC-010 added), CHK013 (FR-SURF-011 made testable), CHK014
(execution treatments enumerated and cited), CHK065 (constitution v3.1.0 change-to-category mapping)
and CHK070 (all eight deferrals now carry a *Revisit when* condition). Each carries a dated closing
note inline.

**One item remains open: CHK042**, specification open item OQ-08. It is not closable here — closing it
locally would invent upstream architecture.

Two mechanical checks were run in support of this review:

- **Identifier integrity (CHK080)**: 156 `FR-` identifiers are defined in `spec.md`. Every `FR-` and
  `SC-` citation in `tasks.md`, `plan.md`, `data-model.md`, `quickstart.md`, `contracts/` and the
  checklists resolves to a defined identifier — **zero dangling citations**.
- **Retention consistency (CHK019)**: the windows in `spec.md` (FR-SESS-007, FR-AUDIT-004,
  FR-AUDIT-005), `data-model.md` §Retention summary and ADR-0003 agree — chat 90 days from terminal
  state, audit 7 years, checkpoints 30 days after completion.

The single open item is neither a CRITICAL issue nor an architecture contradiction.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` were identified by inspecting the current spec; they are
  starting points for review, not confirmed defects
- *2026-09-15*: all `§FR-` references were re-verified against the spec after six feedback
  requirements were inserted. Several were stale or incorrect and have been corrected. The separation
  items now cite `plan.md` and ADR-0001 rather than the spec, because the spec is deliberately
  technology-agnostic and states no requirement about deployables — see CHK080 on identifier stability
- Add findings inline beneath an item rather than editing the item text
